authors: Kokubu, Y., Hara, S. & Tani, A.
title: Mapping seasonal tree canopy cover and leaf area using Worldview-2/3 satellite imagery: A megacity-scale case study in Tokyo urban area
relevance: Quantifies how URBAN canopy cover itself changes with season at city scale, rather than treating season as a nuisance - the number our 18-acquisition series needs and does not have. Directly relevant because our acquisition dates are unknown (Q19) and a leaf-off or shoulder-season year would show genuinely less deciduous canopy, which our pipeline would score as model recall failure. Establishes that seasonal canopy variation in a city is large enough to matter for exactly the comparisons we are making across years.

authors: Kou, R., Fang, B., Chen, G. & Wang, L.
title: Progressive domain adaptation for change detection using season-varying remote sensing images
relevance: Treats seasonal difference as a DOMAIN SHIFT to be aligned before change detection, rather than as noise - the framing our temporal pipeline needs, since we currently attribute every cross-year difference to canopy change or model error with no seasonal term at all. Its core problem statement is ours: real change and seasonally-induced change are hard to separate with a single end-to-end model. Useful as the argument for adding an explicit seasonal/phenological factor to the per-crown validity intervals rather than hoping augmentation absorbs it.
